subject: Observability: retention credit bridge & bundle packaging clarification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Sarah — attaching the proposal we reviewed on the call. Key points called out up front:
- Advanced dashboards + tracing: included in the Ops Insights package (flat monthly slab).
- Retention: tiered buckets; we recommend the 90/365 combo based on your query volumes.
- One-time transition credit (to offset historical ingestion spike) — proposed: $25k in usage credits applied over the first 3 months.

Two asks for you: 1) confirm the dashboard scope (page examples in the deck) and 2) confirm procurement cadence so we can align SOW dates.

Attachments: redwood-observability-proposal-v3.pdf, SOW-Atlas-Health-v2.docx

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0189

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, SecOps Team <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Thanks Ben — review notes below after a quick pass: 
- The dashboards look good; primary ask is an SLA around trace ingestion latency for the real-time alerts (we need <2s for our critical alerts).
- The transition credit is appreciated, but procurement is asking if that can be structured as a "retention bridge" that offsets our increased ingest for the first 60 days rather than a lump credit.
- Also need a clearer breakdown of long-term unit economics (per GB/month after tier) — procurement will want that for their financial model.

Looping in procurement & secops for technical and contracting questions.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Director, Data Platform | Atlas Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Sarah — great questions. Quick answers: 
1) Trace ingestion SLA: we can commit to a pipeline-level p95 of 2s for traces routed through our low-latency ingest path.
   - That path requires prefix-caching and a small reserved burst on Dedicated for the first 3 months; we modeled the cost in the attached pricing tab.
2) Retention bridge: we can convert the one-time credit into a time-bound bridging credit that scales with actual ingest over the first 60 days; suggested cap $30k.
3) Unit economics: attached worksheet with per-GB tiers and expected amortized cost after quantization and KV caching.

Proposal update: convert $25k flat credit -> $30k dynamic bridge (applied prorata to overage for first 60 days), plus explicit SLA clause for trace p95. 

If procurement is comfortable with that structure, I'll need final sign-off from our finance manager for the bridge wording (legal prefers explicit caps).

Ben

From: SecOps Team <secops@atlashealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Ben/Sarah — quick SecOps notes: 
- We'll need details on encryption-at-rest key rotation and SOC 2 evidence for the trace retention store — can you include a short security appendix?
- Also want to understand retention purge guarantees for PHI-tagged traces (compliance requirement).

Please include Marissa from the product team for scope confirmation.

Thanks,
Atlas SecOps

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Atlas Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, SecOps Team <secops@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Hi all — Evelyn from Commercial Ops here. Ben looped me in to speed approvals. Two things from our side to unblock quickly: 
1) Concession framework: we can approve a time-bound retention bridge up to $30k, structured as usage credits applied to ingestion overage for the first 60 days. Conditions: a) SOW signed within 30 days of this agreement, b) credits expire after the 60-day window and are non-refundable.
2) SLA language: we will attach an operational appendix committing to p95 ingestion latency <2s for traces routed through the low-latency path. That appendix will include a fallback carve-out if Atlas requests nonstandard retention/purge semantics for PHI (those require a separate compliance addendum).

Action items for Atlas: please confirm acceptance of the two bullets above so procurement and legal can finalize the SOW. For SecOps: Ben and Marissa will deliver the short security appendix (SOC 2 pointers + key rotation notes) by EOD tomorrow.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
evelyn@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@atlashealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, SecOps Team <secops@atlashealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability package + retention options (proposal attached)

Evelyn — thanks, that structure is workable. Procurement: please proceed with the SOW using the bridge/cap language below. SecOps: Ben/Marissa, we'll expect the security appendix and the PHI purge note by EOD tomorrow; procurement flagged the per-GB post-tier rates as a gating input for finance but the bridge covers our immediate ramp.

We accept the $30k bridge applied prorata over 60 days and the p95 trace SLA for the low-latency path, subject to the SOW and security appendix.

Thanks all — Sarah
